LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.codebookOutputLaw: Draw M length-n codewords independently from the word law q. For a fixed message m, send its codeword through K. The codebook–output law is the joint distribution of the entire sampled codebook and the resulting output word.
Under the random-codebook experiment at message m, the sent codeword and the output have joint distribution q(x)K(y|x).

For a message index j distinct from the sent index m, the competing codeword and the output are independent. Their joint distribution is the product of q and the output law obtained by passing q through K.
Given a codebook b with M ≥ 1 entries and an acceptance set A of word pairs, encode m as b(m). The decoder returns the least index j for which (b(j),y) lies in A, or index zero if no such j exists.
If (b(m),y) belongs to A and (b(j),y) lies outside A for every j ≠ m, decoding y using codebook b and acceptance set A returns m.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mean_codebookOutp: Draw M ≥ 1 codewords independently from q, use the n-fold memoryless channel W and decode by acceptance set A. Averaging the random-codebook error probability over uniformly chosen messages gives the same value as averaging each realized code’s uniform-message error over the distribution of books.
